items.q: Flashes, shower of floaters and spreading curtain with preserved centre is which emergency?
o: Macula on rhegmatogenous detachment needing same day surgery
items.exp: Attached macula dies within hours to days once fluid reaches it; emergency buckle or vitrectomy preserves reading vision while delay sacrifices centre.
items.kp: Curtain with centre spared: save macula tonight.

items.q: Lattice degeneration with atrophic holes in a myope is managed how?
o: Prophylactic barrage laser to holes and lattice
items.exp: Thin lattice with holes tears readily, especially before cataract surgery or in fellow eyes of detachment; laser welds retina preventing spread.
items.kp: Lattice holes in myope: weld them shut.

items.q: Tented immobile detachment with concave surface in proliferative diabetic is which type?
items.exp: Fibrovascular membranes contract pulling retina without primary break; peeling with tamponade flattens while laser alone never releases traction.
items.kp: Tented retina in diabetic: peel the membranes.

items.q: Shifting subretinal fluid without breaks in hypertensive crisis with disc swelling is which detachment?
o: Exudative settling with systemic pressure control
items.exp: Choroidal hyperpermeability oozes beneath retina; urgent pressure lowering reattaches while surgery finds no break to fix.
items.kp: Fluid shifting with crisis pressure: exudative.

items.q: Night blindness with bone spicule pigmentation and tunnel fields in teenager suggests what?
o: Retinitis pigmentosa with ERG and genetics
items.exp: Rod degeneration announces night failure years before fields tunnel; Usher linkage asks hearing while RPE65 testing rescues rare children with gene therapy.
items.kp: Bone spicules plus night blind: RP.

items.q: X linked boy with spoke wheel macula and peripheral schisis cavities has what and course?
o: Juvenile retinoschisis observing unless haemorrhage or detachment
items.exp: Splitting inner layers hollows silently; vitreous veils with bleeding need vitrectomy while uncomplicated cases watch with protection from trauma.
items.kp: Spoke wheel macula in boy: schisis watches.

items.q: Plus disease in retinopathy of prematurity means what and triggers what?
o: Dilated tortuous posterior vessels signalling aggressive disease needing urgent laser
items.exp: Plus marks shunt driven activity preceding traction; peripheral ablation within days aborts detachment while anti VEGF suits selected zone I disease.
items.kp: Preemie plus vessels: laser within days.

o: Under about 32 weeks or 1500 g with oxygen exposure per protocol
items.exp: Immature vessels arrest with oxygen swings; timed retinal exams catch ridge before traction while neonatology titrates oxygen balancing lungs and eyes.
items.kp: Tiny preemie on oxygen: screen retina on schedule.

items.q: Pneumatic retinopexy suits which detachment pattern?
o: Superior single break with laser or cryo plus gas bubble and posturing
items.exp: Gas tamponades superior breaks closed in clinic selected cases; inferior, multiple or tractional disease needs buckle or vitrectomy. Posturing compliance decides.
items.kp: Single top break: bubble it shut.

items.q: Silicone oil tamponade differs from gas chiefly by which practical points?
o: No posturing or altitude limits but needs later removal surgery with emulsification risks
items.exp: Oil holds inferior and complex repairs without positioning, but cataract, glaucoma and keratopathy accumulate until removal; gas self absorbs with strict compliance.
items.kp: Oil holds without posture but must come out.
